notes:
ACCURACY: 25 sampled (random.seed(7) over the 128 harvest brands): 14 AAPS, 7 Tucson Fine Mineral Gallery, 3 Mineralogical Record Label Archive, 1 Purdue. All 25 names appear on their src pages (all four pages re-fetched raw). 1 wrong: Dreher Carvings is a gemstone-carving exhibitor, outside the F6 test. Tier fixes (not counted as errors because the 'says' text is honest): all 13 Tucson rows and all 4 meteorite.com rows carry layer 'premium' on existence-only pages: set tier 'listed'. The 83 AAPS rows carry layer 'premium': per the coordinator ruling they are 'cultural' (ethics-bound professional association), not premium. Get Stuffed rests only on its own page: 'listed'. Coober Pedy Dale Price Opals: existence only, 'listed'.
LABEL ARCHIVE CAVEAT: all 16 copied names checked against the raw index text and against the Label Archive inventory PDF; all are real firms, not persons. Two need fixing: 'Bayerisches Petrefacten und Mineralien' is truncated (page: 'Bayerisches Petrefacten und Mineralien Comptoir'); 'Mineral Cabinet, The' is the index's inverted form (use 'The Mineral Cabinet', New Providence NJ). Most are historic or closed firms: mark status historic. The archive only proves a firm left labels; it supports historic presence, not quality.
HOMONYMS: Carolina Biological Supply Co. is not register 'Carolina' (A2 work boots): homonym:true. Ward's Natural Science Establishment and NASCO have no register clash. Pala International (gem and mineral dealer) is not in the register at all; if A3 adds it, cross_tag. Mineral Kingdom of Woodmere must keep its qualifier (distinct from the Houston dealer Mineral Kingdom). Fabre Minerals is unrelated to Marius Fabre and Gael Fabre. Heritage Auctions (F2) is the same company: cross_tag F6 (added as a cross_tag row). Fine Minerals International appeared only in a harvest region list, never as a brand row: now added.
CITES / LEGALITY NOTES NEEDED: Antonino De Simone and the Torre del Greco coral region (Corallium; Pacific precious corals are on CITES Appendix III); Deyrolle and Get Stuffed (taxidermy, shells, coral); historic trophy houses already in the register (Rowland Ward, Van Ingen & Van Ingen, Tocher and Tocher, Edward Gerrard & Sons: tiger, big-game, ivory: Appendix I taxa, antique-ivory rules); Skulls Unlimited, Valley Anatomical Preparations, The Evolution Store, Wunderkammer Zurich (skulls, skeletons, taxidermy); The Bug House, BugsDirect-type insect sellers, Mushi-sha (birdwing butterflies Ornithoptera/Troides, Teinopalpus, Bhutanitis: Appendix I/II); shell sellers Conchology Inc. and Femorale (Tridacnidae giant clams, queen conch, Nautilidae, black and stony corals: Appendix II). Fossil ivory (mammoth) is not CITES but is banned by several US states (AAPS's own 'Fossil Ivory Ban' page): add a state-law note to any AAPS dealer selling it. Minerals, meteorites, fossils and amber are not CITES, but national export and heritage laws apply (Morocco, China, Brazil, Mongolia dinosaur material).
IMCA: the harvest said the IMCA member list is login-restricted. It is public (imcax.com memberlist, 513 members, persons with country; per-member pages sometimes give a website). It confirms Geoffrey Notkin (member since 2006, Aerolite Meteorites, AAPS row) and Bruno Fectay (since 2010, La Memoire de la Terre, AAPS row); many Moroccan and Australian members. Firm names are rarely given, so it is weak for new brands (only Treasure Coast Meteorite Co., member since 2026: not added).
THIN AREAS RETRIED: shells (Conchology Inc., Femorale added; Schooner Specimen Shells only on a dealer list, existence only, not added); entomology (Mushi-sha, Shiga Konchu Fukyusha added; BugsDirect and Watkins & Doncaster only on their own pages, not added; Insect Designs and The Bugmaniac not found); display (Riker mount origin traced to Clarence B. Riker's 1902 patent, the generic mount has no maker brand; only self-described cabinet makers such as Chadwick End Cabinets (UK) and commodity suppliers found: nothing distinctive); taxidermy (three studios recorded as 'listed' self-claims: Martin Berndt (DE), Praeparator Raith (AT), Border Taxidermy Studios (UK); the European Taxidermy Championships and the Guild publish no studio award list); Sainte-Marie (live exhibitor page sainte-marie-mineral.com/en/exhibitors-list shows only sponsors; no award list exists publicly); Munich (no award list; 2026 magazine PDF lists special-show lenders only); Dalnegorsk (Wikipedia page fetched: no specimen renown stated, not recorded); Japan (insect-collecting culture added; suiseki rivers added); China (scholar's-rock region added); Russia (Kaliningrad amber); Southeast Asia (Mogok, Ratnapura, Conchology Inc. in Cebu); Oceania (Lightning Ridge black opal); Northern Europe and Middle East (Baltic amber; Iranian material via Via Mineralia; Lebanon is already covered by Memory of Time in AAPS). Latin America: Muzo emeralds, Femorale.
REGIONS NOT QUOTAS: element samples and display supplies are a small global niche (one search each, nothing regional). Ruby, emerald and opal regions are recorded without makers because their fetched pages name no firm.
MAIN BLIND SPOTS: (1) the harvest's premium tier rests almost entirely on existence-only lists (AAPS, Tucson, meteorite.com); real quality evidence for the mineral summit (Krantz, Fine Minerals International, Fabre, MinRec editorial picks) has now been added, but Kristalle, Collector's Edge, Crystal Classics and Wilensky still lack independent quality pages in the harvest (the Tucson gallery PDF tucsonfineminerals.com/TFMG_2026.pdf has self-written profiles only); (2) gem cutters and cut-stone houses (Idar-Oberstein, Bangkok/Chanthaburi, Jaipur) are absent: probably A3's job, but loose cut gems are in F6; (3) no Chinese, Russian or Latin American dealer brands with independent pages (Chinese dealers appear in MinRec show reports behind the paywall); (4) entomology and shells are still seller-led with few independent sources.
SOURCES: all additions rest on fetched pages; several were read in excerpt mode (Parallel web_fetch without full_content) where the page was long: AA (amber), D&S Times (Whitby), Nakano city, VSANA, Wikipedia gongshi/Mogok/Ratnapura/Muzo/Lightning Ridge, MinRec online report, studio home pages. Raw saves: AUDIT_F6_tmp/raw/ (Poppe Wikipedia, IMCA member list).
